title: finding(plugin-grid): clicking a column header sends `$orderby` as an array of `{field, order}` objects, a shape the protocol's `odata.zod.ts` does not declare — it declares `string | string[]`
body:
Measured by the `domain:spec` @ objectui PM seat while producing the server-contract measurement
objectui#8961 was blocked on, `2026-09-15T03:08Z`–`03:09Z`.
objectui `origin/main` = `b7479abc74100e022b5f1233fd14d4fabc891788`; objectstack `origin/main` = `b3b43b6ea0`.
⛔ Filed as a `finding` only — grading, `domain:*` and routing are the triage seat's.

## The defect

When a user clicks a column header, `object-grid` sends `$orderby` as an **array of objects**:

```
params.$orderby = headerSort.map((s) => ({ field: s.field, order: s.order }));
```
(`packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`, the `headerSort` arm.)

The protocol declares `$orderby` as a **string or an array of strings**, and nothing else —
`objectstack` `packages/spec/src/api/odata.zod.ts`, verbatim:

```ts
$orderby: z.union([
  z.string(),           // "name desc"
  z.array(z.string()),  // ["name desc", "email asc"]
]).optional().describe('Sort order'),
```

`packages/spec/src/api/query-adapter.zod.ts` carries only a doc example in the same string form
(`$orderby=name asc`) and declares no second shape.

⇒ **an array of `{ field, order }` objects is not a declared value of this key.**

## The three shapes one component family puts on one key

| producer | shape | declared by the protocol |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `object-grid` array arm (`toOrderByClause`) | `"field order"` join string | ✅ **yes** |
| `object-grid` `headerSort` arm | `[{ field, order }]` object array | ❌ **no** |
| shared sink `convertSortToQueryParams` (`@object-ui/core`) | `Record<string, 'asc' \| 'desc'>` map | ❌ **no** |

⭐ The join string — the one repeatedly described in this repo as `object-grid`'s *private*
lowering — is the only one of the three the protocol actually declares. That framing is worth
correcting wherever it appears.

## Why this is filed rather than folded into objectui#8961

objectui#8961 is the header-arrow reader, and it is now in the decision inbox carrying this same
server-contract measurement. This card is the **writer** on the other side of the same key, and it
is a different question: #8961 asks what the arrow may parse, this asks what the grid may send.

objectui#8973's pin names this arm and calls it *"a documented, deliberate difference, not a
defect"*. ⚠️ **Deliberate and declared are not the same property.** That sentence records an
intention; it does not record a protocol reading, and the protocol reading above did not exist when
it was written.

## ⚠️ What is NOT measured, and it is the half that decides the grading

**Whether the server actually accepts the object array.** This seat read the protocol
**declaration** only — ⛔ not the driver, the runtime parser, or any request log. Two outcomes, and
they point opposite ways:

- the server **refuses or silently ignores** it ⇒ clicking a column header produces an unordered
  result set, which is a user-visible defect of the same family as objectui#8961;
- the server **accepts** it ⇒ the protocol is declared **narrower than the implementation**, and
  under the maintainer's standing principle 「协议不正确的应该先修改协议」 the repair is an
  objectstack spec card **first**, ⛔ not an objectui change.

Whoever takes this owes that reading before proposing either direction.

Dedup: searched before filing; objectui#8961 (the reader half, in the decision inbox),
objectui#5270 / #5293 / #3950 (all closed, all about `sort` shapes on the authoring side, none about
the wire value of `$orderby`). The search's must-hit control returned #8961 itself, so the empty
result is a reading rather than a broken query.
